text:
natalie: Heads up — I'm seeing a cluster of ECC correctable spikes from a subset of cards in us-west-2b over the last ~3h. Not uniform across the rack; some cards show tiny blips, a few have repeated bursts. Want to avoid knee-jerk drains. Thoughts on a robust detection + remediation rule?

mike: Can you paste the grafana panel or the raw query? want to see per-gpu distribution.

natalie: Query I used: ```sum by(gpu_id)(increase(nv_gpu_ecc_correctable_total[5m]))``` panel: https://grafana.redwood/inbox/abcdef (private). Output shows 0-1 typical, but 3 GPUs hit 12-18 in 5m windows in two separate bursts.

jess: My 2c: move from absolute-rate thresholds to a signal-to-noise approach. Compute baseline mean/stddev over last 7d per-card and flag when current 5m rate > mean + k * stddev. k=4-6 tends to catch real degradation vs noise.

siva: +1 for SNR. Also propose evidence buckets so we don't immediately replace on one burst:
- burst: single 5m window > SNR threshold but not sustained
- sustained: 3/4 consecutive 5m windows > threshold
- trend: daily rate increasing (slope test over 24h)
Each bucket maps to different actions (alert, soft-evac, replace queue).

mike: Policy sketch:
- burst -> create Inc alert to eng-infra channel + tag owner; monitor 30m
- sustained -> auto-soft-evac (soft drain, migration but keep node for 2h bake window)
- trend (sustained across 24h) -> mark for hardware replace/RAID swap and schedule ticket
We should set soft-evac TTL so we don't keep shrinking capacity forever. Suggested bake window: 2h soft-evac; if errors stop -> un-evac. If continue -> escalate.

jess: Implementation notes: we can implement SNR as: ```SNR = (rate_5m - mean_24h) / stddev_24h``` and alert when SNR >= 5. Use a rolling mean/std that excludes maintenance windows.

infra-bot: [alert-summary] 3 GPUs in cluster us-west-2b exceeded burst threshold at 2025-09-13T18:12:00Z. IDs: gpu-uw2b-17, gpu-uw2b-19, gpu-uw2b-23.

siva: Driver/firmware confounders: before we auto-replace, check for recent kernel/driver pushes and host-side soft errors (ECC retry logs). If we see coincident deploy, mark as "deploy-suspected" and increase bake window to 6h.

mike: Cost tradeoff: replacing hardware = ~$2k per card + downtime. Auto-replacing too eagerly increases ops cost. Prefer multi-signal confirmation: SNR + sustained + driver-diff OR elevated Xid10 errors.

jess: Also add an evidence score: each signal adds points: SNR burst=2, sustained=4, driver-diff=3, Xid errors=3. If score >=7 -> create replace ticket automatically. Keeps policy readable.

natalie: Good. Two extra asks: 1) add a PromQL expression we can ship to alert manager; 2) add a small dashboard tile showing per-gpu bake window state (normal / soft-evac / marked-for-replace).

mike: PromQL suggestion (placeholder): ```
# per-gpu SNR
mu = avg_over_time(increase(nv_gpu_ecc_correctable_total[5m])[24h:5m])
sd = stddev_over_time(increase(nv_gpu_ecc_correctable_total[5m])[24h:5m])
SNR = (increase(nv_gpu_ecc_correctable_total[5m]) - mu) / sd
SNR > 5
```

siva: For rollout: enable SNR alerts in canary cluster first (us-west-1a) for 48h, tune k, then flip on us-west-2b. Also add an annotation to auto-soft-evac events with reason and SNR value for postmortem.

infra-bot: Created ticket INF-4721: "Implement ECC SNR-based detection + soft-evac policy (canary)" assigned to @mike.

jess: small UX: when we soft-evac, emit a lightweight notification to affected team's slack channel so model owners can evaluate perf impact. also log token-cost delta for that node.

mike: I'll prototype alert rule + evidence scoring today. Can we agree on initial params for the canary? proposal: k=5 (SNR), sustained = 3 consecutive 5m windows, soft-evac TTL = 2h, replacement score threshold = 7.

natalie: Agreed to those canary params. I'll own the dashboard tile and runbook note.

siva: I'll add driver-deploy correlation logic to the alert pipeline.

mike: timeline: prototype + unit tests by EOD, canary deploy next Tue.

natalie: Thanks all — appreciate the practical compromise (avoid noisy drains, still automated when evidence is strong). Will follow up with links to the new dashboard and the ticket. :thumbsup:
